vision_question: Does the AI HBM cycle hold for the next 5 years?

feasibility.rationale: AI compute demand pull is real; HBM yield + Korea export concentration are the binding constraints.

capabilities.name: AI HBM demand durability
capabilities.description: Sustained HBM consumption per AI training+inference deployment over 5 years.
capabilities.rationale: Without sustained demand, ASP collapses on the next supply step-up — historical commodity DRAM pattern.

score.rationale: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guides intact; inference share growing.

capabilities.name: HBM3/HBM4 yield curve
capabilities.description: Stack yield improvement rate from HBM3e → HBM4 → HBM4e.
capabilities.rationale: Yield directly determines net supply; binding constraint on industry-wide HBM availability.

score.rationale: SK Hynix HBM4 yield ~50%; Samsung qualification slipping.

capabilities.name: Commodity DRAM pricing power
capabilities.description: ASP cycle for commodity DDR — drives the non-AI half of memory maker P&L.
capabilities.rationale: AI HBM is the headline but commodity DDR still dominates revenue mix.

score.rationale: DDR5 mix lifting blended ASP; smartphone demand soft.

capabilities.name: Node migration execution (1z/1a/1b/1c)
capabilities.description: Memory makers' ability to migrate to leading-edge DRAM nodes on schedule.
capabilities.rationale: Each shrink lowers bit cost ~15%; missed nodes erode margin permanently.

score.rationale: 1c node ramp on schedule at SK Hynix; Samsung 1c uncertain.

capabilities.name: Korea supply chain concentration
capabilities.description: Korea (SK Hynix + Samsung) holds ~70% of global HBM supply.
capabilities.rationale: Geopolitical risk (China tension, US export controls, KR labor strikes) could disrupt the entire HBM supply chain.

score.rationale: Concentration unchanged; regulatory headwinds from US-China tension continue.

capabilities.name: Memory capex efficiency
capabilities.description: Capex required per Gb of incremental capacity. Trending up with EUV intensification.
capabilities.rationale: Higher capex/Gb compresses returns; overinvestment risk on AI cycle ending.

score.rationale: EUV intensity +20% per node; capex discipline tested.

dependencies.rationale: Net supply scarcity sustains ASP — feeds back into demand durability.
Cost-down via node migration shapes commodity DRAM unit economics.
Korea hosts the binding HBM capacity.
Capex efficiency determines whether marginal supply is profitable.

risks.name: US-China export controls on AI memory
risks.description: Tightening US export restrictions on HBM to China could compress demand visibility.
risks.mitigations: Diversify customer mix; comply with allowed-spec carve-outs.

risks.name: Samsung HBM qualification recovery
risks.description: Samsung HBM3e qualification at NVIDIA repeatedly delayed; sustained miss could shift industry HBM share.

risks.name: AI capex compression
risks.description: Hyperscaler capex moderation could compress HBM demand growth to single digits.
risks.mitigations: Diversify into automotive + edge AI memory.

risks.name: Korea single-country logistics disruption
risks.description: Strike, earthquake, or geopolitical event in Korea halts >80% of global HBM shipments for days-to-weeks.
risks.mitigations: Multi-site buffer inventory; US/JP secondary capacity; diplomatic engagement.

risks.name: CoWoS packaging capacity bottleneck
risks.description: TSMC's CoWoS advanced-packaging line is the single chokepoint for HBM-stacked accelerator shipments; capacity expansion lagging demand.
risks.mitigations: Alternative packaging (SoIC, ABF substrates); diversified packaging partners (Intel Foundry); inventory buffering.
